analysis.summary: Germany enter this Round of 32 clash as heavy favourites having topped Group E with 6 points and a +7 goal difference (7-1 vs Curacao, 2-1 vs Ivory Coast, 2-1 loss to Ecuador when rotation was possible). Paraguay scraped through as one of the best third-placed sides from Group D with 4 points, their sole win a narrow 1-0 over Turkey; they were hammered 4-1 by the USA and drew 0-0 with Australia, averaging just 1.04 xG and 0.7 corners per match. The talent and tactical gap is substantial: Germany's front three of Wirtz, Musiala and Sane are among the tournament's most dangerous, while Paraguay's collective attacking output across three games amounted to a single goal from open play.
analysis.home_form: Won Group E with 6 points: W 7-1 Curacao (Jun 14), W 2-1 Ivory Coast (Jun 20), L 2-1 Ecuador (Jun 25, with heavy rotation possible). Germany averaged 2.23 xG per match, 17.7 shots and 6 corners per game in the group stage. The 4-2-3-1 under Nagelsmann with Wirtz, Musiala, Sane behind Havertz has been fluid and high-scoring.
analysis.away_form: Paraguay finished third in Group D with 4 points: L 4-1 USA (Jun 12), W 1-0 Turkey (Jun 19), D 0-0 Australia (Jun 25). Gustavo Alfaro's side sit in a compact defensive block, allowing minimal space and relying on set pieces and transitions. They averaged only 1.04 xG and 3.3 box shots per game, generating almost no corner volume (0.7 per match).
analysis.h2h: Germany and Paraguay have met three times. Most notably, Germany eliminated Paraguay 1-0 in the 2002 World Cup Round of 16 (Oliver Neuville 88th minute). The teams also met in a 2013 friendly. Germany have the upper hand in the historical record. This will be their first competitive meeting since 2002.
injuries_news: Germany CB Nico Schlotterbeck ruled out for the tournament with a torn ankle ligament sustained against Ivory Coast; Antonio Rudiger and Jonathan Tah expected to start at centre-back.
Germany LB Nathaniel Brown carrying a groin concern but projected to start.
Paraguay CM Diego Gomez suspended after accumulating two yellow cards in the group stage; he was the primary set-piece and penalty taker, a significant loss.
Paraguay RW Ramon Sosa (muscle) and CB Omar Alderete (knee) both doubtful and need to be assessed.
Paraguay MF Miguel Almiron returns from suspension and is expected to feature.
key_factors: Paraguay's suspension of Diego Gomez weakens their midfield engine and their set-piece threat — their primary corner and free-kick taker is absent.
Germany's pressing system and wing overloads should expose Paraguay's low defensive block over 90 minutes, with Wirtz and Musiala capable of cutting inside from narrow positions.

Paraguay's counter-attack via Enciso and Almiron is their primary attacking outlet; Germany must track runners behind the high line — Rudiger's pace is adequate but the defensive reorganisation post-Schlotterbeck adds a slight vulnerability.

Referee Jalal Jayed (Morocco) averages approximately 4.57 yellow cards per game, placing him as a stricter-than-average official; Paraguay's physical, combative style could see them accumulate bookings.
Germany average 6 corners per match vs Paraguay's 0.7 — corner volume likely to be heavily one-sided and total corners in this match should skew well under the typical 9.5 line.

Paraguay's entire group-stage goal tally was one goal (the 4-1 loss included a rare situation vs the USA hosts); BTTS probability is low given Paraguay's inability to score against organised defences.
